blind_target.authors: Busner J, Youngstrom EA, Langfus JA, et al.
blind_target.title: Replicating and extending the reliability, criterion validity, and treatment sensitivity of the shortened PANSS for pediatric trials.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The results presented in this study evaluated these optimized forms in data from an additional independent randomized pediatric schizophrenia trial (Savitz et al., 2015 ). Overall, these results support three previous studies showing that the PANSS10 and PANSS20 compare favorably to the 30-item PANSS in terms of content coverage, reliability, validity, and calibration, with a significant reduction in administration length (Busner et al., 2024 ; Findling et al., 2023 ; Youngstrom et al., 2024 ).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Overall, these results support three previous studies showing that the PANSS10 and PANSS20 compare favorably to the 30-item PANSS in terms of content coverage, reliability, validity, and calibration, with a significant reduction in administration length (Busner et al., 2024 ; Findling et al., 2023 ; Youngstrom et al., 2024 ).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors state an overall supportive verdict explicitly covering all three prior studies.

luna_triage.reason: The introduction specifies the prior Busner calibration result and explicitly says the present work is its first replication. Shipped row 630 is Findling et al. (2023), the initial development of the optimized PANSS forms, not the Busner 2024 calibration finding.
luna_triage.omission_quote: In our most recent work (Busner et al., 2024 ), we examined the calibration of the optimized forms against the full-length version at common study inclusion thresholds (i.e., equivalent to full-length PANSS scores of 60 and 120) and found that the optimized forms showed minimal discrepancies compared with the 30-item form. The current work presents the first replication of this important finding, again using multisite international clinical trial data. In addition to examining these inclusion thresholds, the current work evaluates the performance of the PANSS10 and PANSS20 short forms in terms of measurement model fit, reliability of the scores, and content coverage relative to the PANSS30.
